decision: Kept the existing Dashboard behavior and CSS variables while moving shared chrome into the root layout.
reason: The new route needs shared navigation without redesigning the homepage.
result: Source baseline recorded; web checks not run.

decision: Used one ordered DEAL_STAGES registry and the API's grouped board response.
reason: One source controls stage values, labels, column order, and empty columns.

decision: Routed native drag and drop and the stage select through one moveDeal operation.
reason: Both interactions must share PATCH behavior, pending state, error handling, and post-success state updates.

decision: Used the demo user from GET /auth/me as the visible owner on every deal card.
reason: The API has no deal owner relation, so owner initials are explicit mock data rather than inferred account data.
result: Implemented as Demo User initials with accessible owner text; web checks pending.

decision: Accepted the lead's verified API unit as the frontend contract baseline.
reason: The board UI depends on stable ordered columns and persisted PATCH stage changes.
evidence: Lead-provided pytest and live HTTP results
result: pytest 10 passed; seeded counts 5/4/4/4/4/4; PATCH deal 1 persisted in qualified; invalid stage returned 422.

decision: Configured Vitest's Oxc JSX transform instead of adding a React Vite plugin.
reason: The latest plugin requires TypeScript syntax that this Next 14 project does not support.
result: Vitest parsed TSX and the project typechecked without changing the app's TypeScript version.

decision: Resolved a missing native drop event from the pointer position during dragend and guarded against duplicate updates.
reason: Chrome cleared the nested drag target and reported no drop even while the pointer remained over the destination column.
result: Real Chrome drag moved Summit Energy Revenue workspace and regression tests cover missing-drop and duplicate-drop paths.

decision: Ran the final automated web checks after cleaning all debug instrumentation.
reason: The interaction, type, lint, and production routes must pass together.
evidence: pnpm test, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint, pnpm build
result: 3 Vitest tests passed; typecheck and lint passed; production build generated /deals/board.

decision: Re-ran the API suite after the final web drag fix.
reason: The frontend fix must not weaken the stage contract.
result: 10 API tests passed with one existing Starlette deprecation warning.

decision: Verified native drag, the stage select fallback, and hard-refresh persistence against the running UI and API.
reason: Compile checks do not prove browser events or SQLite persistence.
result: Select moved a card and persisted; mouse drag moved Summit Energy Revenue workspace from Closed Lost to Closed Won; hard refresh kept Closed Won with counts 5 and 4.

decision: Saved the absent-route baseline and completed board state.
reason: The PR requires running-app before and after screenshots.
result: Before shows the /deals/board 404; after shows six populated columns and the persisted moved card.

decision: Unified drop and dragend behind one synchronous completion guard and preserved nested-column acceptance.
reason: Independent review found the earlier two-flag drag lifecycle harder to prove idempotent.
result: 3 Vitest tests passed; typecheck, lint, and production build passed; reviewed Chrome drag persisted after hard refresh.
